questions.prompt: What is the rationale field on a change request actually for?
questions.explanation: It's the project's memory. In six months, when someone asks why a part has a notch in it, the rationale is the only place that answer still exists — the people who knew have graduated.

answers.text: To record why the change was made, for whoever asks in six months
To justify the change to the faculty advisor
To let the system estimate how long the change will take
It's optional paperwork with no downstream use

questions.prompt: How does Constellation work out which items a change request affects?
questions.explanation: From the BOM. Assemblies know which parts and versions they reference, so the impact list is derived rather than remembered — which is exactly the kind of thing people get wrong under deadline pressure.

answers.text: From the BOM — it derives what references the changed item
The person raising it lists the affected items manually
It notifies everyone on the project and lets them self-identify
It scans the project's Drive folder for related files

questions.prompt: A reviewer rejects your change request. What happens to it?
questions.explanation: It stays, with the reason recorded. That record is the value — the next person to propose the same change can see why it was turned down, instead of relitigating a decision nobody remembers making.

answers.text: It stays in the record with the reviewer's reason attached
It's deleted so the list stays clean
It reopens automatically after a week
It's converted into a task assigned back to you

questions.prompt: What happens when a change request is approved? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: Approval is what makes a change real: the item takes its new version, the BOM updates, and holders of affected downstream parts are notified. It does not touch anyone's XP — CRs are a review process, not a reward event.

answers.text: The affected item takes its new version
Members holding affected downstream items are notified
The requester is granted XP for the approval
All linked tasks are automatically closed

questions.prompt: Rejecting a change request is a sign the review process has failed.
questions.explanation: False. "Not until after the design review" is a perfectly good outcome, and a team that only ever approves has stopped reviewing. Rejection with a written reason is the process working.
